evidence: Lighthouse (mobile, score 82) lists this icon under 'Image elements do not have [alt] attributes'. Screenshot: screenshots/lighthouse-missing-alt.png
user_impact: Screen-reader users cannot tell what the accessibility control does, so the page's own accessibility tools are unusable for them.
recommended_fix: Add alt text (for example 'Accessibility options') or an aria-label on the control.

evidence: The Tamil switch is a picture of text with no alt attribute, listed in the same Lighthouse audit. Screenshot: screenshots/lighthouse-missing-alt.png
user_impact: Screen-reader users cannot find the language switch; users who enlarge text get a blurry, non-scaling image.
recommended_fix: Replace with real text 'தமிழ்' in a link with lang="ta".

evidence: Listed as missing alt in Lighthouse. Screenshot: screenshots/lighthouse-missing-alt.png
user_impact: Screen-reader users get no description (or hear a file name) for the banner.
recommended_fix: Add a short descriptive alt, or alt="" if purely decorative.

evidence: Decorative bullet images beside list entries have no alt attribute. Screenshot: screenshots/lighthouse-missing-alt-2.png
user_impact: Screen readers may announce a file name before every list item, adding noise.
recommended_fix: Mark decorative images alt="" or use CSS list-style / background images.

page_or_component: Links across the home page (architecture / content)
evidence: Lighthouse flags 'Links do not have a discernible name'. Taken together with WEB-001 to 004, missing text alternatives point to no shared component or content template enforcing alt text and link names. (Root cause is an inference, not verified in source.)
user_impact: Screen-reader users hear only 'link' with no purpose.
recommended_fix: Shared Link and Image components that require text alternatives (this repo's first vertical slice enforces labelled controls).
